title: Model onboarding cards with embedded performance inspector and pin confirmation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design a compact, card-based onboarding surface that lets users inspect a model version's published performance profile inline, create a deterministic pin (commit snapshot) to a route, and confirm rollout parameters without leaving the onboarding flow. The goal is to reduce cognitive context-switching between the model catalog and the routing/pinning flow, make performance data discoverable at the moment of decision, and provide strong affordances for safe rollouts (canary %, rollback path, test traffic). The surface will be used in hosted, dedicated, and private console instances.
background: Current console flows split model browsing, performance profile publishing, and version pinning into separate modal or page contexts. Product analytics show drop-off when engineers attempt to pin a model while validating latency/cost trade-offs. This design iterates on a single-surface flow that combines a model card, an inline performance inspector (snapshot of latency, p50/p95, token-cost, memory footprint), and a pin confirmation panel with rollout controls and audit metadata capture.
design_goals: Make performance signals immediately visible during pin decisions
Reduce clicks to pin a version to a route to <= 3
Provide clear rollback and canary controls by default
Surface provenance (who published the performance profile, when, and dataset used)
Keyboard accessible and screen-reader friendly interactions
acceptance_criteria: Model card lists available versions and highlights which have a published performance profile
Clicking a version expands an inline inspector showing p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit rate, and memory/VRAM footprint
Pin confirmation panel allows selecting: pin type (hard pin / traffic split / fallback), initial canary percentage, automatic rollback threshold, and scheduled start time
Publishing a performance profile is available inline via a 'Publish profile' button that opens a lightweight wizard and attaches the profile to the version
All interactions have analytics hooks (pin start, pin submit, publish profile, rollback action) documented for instrumentation
Design includes error states and recovery UX for profile publishing failures and insufficient capacity warnings
Design mockups and component specs handed to frontend with annotated keyboard flows and ARIA roles
design_notes: Prefer a compact list view for catalog pages; expand-to-inspect pattern keeps layout stable
Show deltas when comparing current pinned version vs selected version (latency + cost + quality metric)
Use a color-safe indicator for 'published profile age' (green < 2 weeks, amber < 90 days, gray > 90 days)
Default canary to 5% with a recommended automatic rollback at 30% error increase over baseline
Include a 'simulate expected p95 under target traffic' micro-interaction for PMs to test impact
accessibility_considerations: All interactive controls reachable by keyboard in a logical tab order
Inspector charts have text alternatives and numeric tables for screen readers
Contrast and focus styles meet WCAG AA for all states
Provide ARIA labels for pin types and programmatic announcement for successful pin completion
risks_and_open_questions: How to represent quality regressions for subjective metrics (e.g., hallucination) in a concise inspector
Backend API surface for publishing profiles must return a deterministic profile id and timestamp; confirm contract with infra
Telemetry requirements: ensure pin + publish events include model_id, version, route, and commit metadata
Edge case: what happens if capacity is insufficient for a hard pin—should we auto-create a queued reservation or show a recommended dedicated plan?
next_steps: Sync with runtime team (ENG-3012) to finalize profile API contract by 2025-02-18
Validate canary defaults with product and SRE; finalize thresholds
Produce hi-fi mocks for desktop and tablet and hand off to frontend by 2025-02-24
Add analytics tracking spec and event names to the instrumentation doc
